newsitem.title: KENYA: Planes in near collision over Kenya - controllers.
newsitem.headline: Planes in near collision over Kenya - controllers.

text.p: Two planes carrying 126 passengers came within 50 feet (15 metres) of each other near the Kenyan city of Mombasa on the fifth day of a strike by air traffic controllers, controllers said on Thursday.

One plane, a Kenya Airways Fokker Friendship with 58 passengers, had just taken off for Nairobi. The other, an Air Lauda plane with 68 tourists and eight crew, was about to land in Mombasa from Nairobi, said the substitute controllers.

The near collision took place on Wednesday about 86 km (50 miles) from Mombasa at a height of between 18,000 and 19,000 feet (5,400 to 5,800 metres), they added. The controllers asked not to be named.
The air traffic controllers are demanding a 50-fold increase in salaries, to 261,510 shillings ($4,670) a month from 5,000.
The government gave them until Tuesday afternoon to return to work or face dismissal but the controllers defied the order.

The strike has caused long delays in flights because the airports authority does not have enough substitute controllers. It has brought in instructors and administrators, some of whom are out of practice.
The Kenya Airports Authority was not available to comment on the near collision because of a public holiday.
